name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,808

entries.clue: Charles spotting game for kids is easily cracked (6)

indicatorNotes.spotting: Charles is seen next to the game, so CR sits just before it

blocks.note: Carolus Rex, King Charles's royal cipher
I Spy, the children's guessing game

annotation.surface: A man called Charles is caught playing a children's game, and he gives in at once.
annotation.walkthrough: CR is the cipher of a King Charles (Carolus Rex). 'Easily cracked' reads as a comment on Charles; it is the definition, like a crispy biscuit.
annotation.definitionFit: Something crispy snaps or cracks with little pressure.

entries.clue: Feed dog (4)

blocks.note: read as a noun, slang for food or grub
a fluffy Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue

annotation.surface: An instruction to give the dog its dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feed' looks like a verb, but here it is the noun, food, which is what chow means.
annotation.definitionFit: Chow is informal for food, and a chow is a fluffy Chinese dog breed.

entries.clue: Illustration on the outside with name, swinging regularly? (3,4)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter of 'swinging' is taken

blocks.note: with = in, as in 'in company' or 'in love'

annotation.surface: A picture hangs outside with a name on it, swaying back and forth.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a description of the answer, which is the joke, but the wordplay is there: 'swinging' yields its odd letters. British pubs hang a painted sign outside naming the house.
annotation.definitionFit: A pub or inn sign is a named picture hanging outside that swings in the breeze.

entries.clue: Hole having each pro worried (9)

blocks.note: per = each, as in 'a pound per head'
ate = worried, as in 'what's eating you?'

annotation.surface: A gap in which every professional has become anxious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hole' is a verb here: to hole something is to perforate it. 'Worried' as ATE comes from 'eat' meaning to trouble someone.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Hole' used as a verb: to hole a thing, like a ship's hull, is to pierce it through.

entries.clue: Little beauty that woman found in beastly baby (6)

indicatorNotes.found in: to be found in a place is to be located inside it, so HER sits inside CUB

blocks.note: a cub is a baby animal

annotation.surface: A pretty little thing, a woman, discovered inside a young animal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' is not an insult here: it means belonging to a beast, so a beastly baby is a cub.
annotation.definitionFit: A cherub is a sweet, angelic little child: a little beauty.

entries.clue: Animated miner quietly parking in Welsh town for festival (5)

indicatorNotes.in: parking in a town means placing something inside it, so the P's sit within HAY

blocks.note: Hay-on-Wye, home of the Hay literary festival

annotation.surface: A lively coal miner parks silently in a Welsh festival town.
annotation.walkthrough: The miner is a cartoon one: Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's animated Snow White, who work in a mine. Hay-on-Wye is a small Welsh border town famous for its book festival.
annotation.definitionFit: Happy is one of Disney's animated dwarfs, who dig in a mine.

entries.clue: Roger slipped out of bed to consider a fresh approach (7)

indicatorNotes.slipped: ROGER's letters slip out of order

annotation.surface: Roger slides out from under the covers to rethink his plans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slipped out of bed' reads as one phrase, but 'slipped' works alone on Roger and 'out of bed' is UP.
annotation.definitionFit: To regroup is to pause and reorganise before trying again.

entries.clue: Extra large cat receives shocking treatment in scrap for seat (2-8)

indicatorNotes.receives: a thing that receives takes something into itself, so LION holds ECT

blocks.note: a bye is an extra run in cricket
a lion is a large cat

annotation.surface: A huge cat gets electric shocks during a fight over a chair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extra large' looks like XL, but 'Extra' is BYE alone. A by-election is a British vote held mid-term to fill one vacant parliamentary seat.
annotation.definitionFit: A by-election is a contest, or scrap, to fill a single vacant seat.

entries.clue: One might display products in two ways (6,4)

annotation.definition: One might display products in two ways

blocks.note: the surface suggests any shop window or stall
sounds like two methods; the setter means two streets, as a shop on the junction faces both

annotation.surface: A remark about showing goods in two different fashions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Two ways' suggests two methods, but it means two streets: a shop on the corner has frontage on both. In Britain a corner shop is a small local grocery.
annotation.definitionFit: A corner shop sits where two roads meet, so it can display its goods along both.

entries.clue: Large flag inside hotel the colour of mud (11)

blocks.note: the heart is the inside, the core
H = hotel in the NATO alphabet
stone is a pale grey-brown colour

annotation.surface: A big banner hangs inside a mud-coloured hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inside' looks like a container instruction but is a noun giving HEART. A flag here is a flagstone, not a banner.
annotation.definitionFit: A hearthstone is the large flat flagstone forming a fireplace's hearth.

entries.clue: Celt moving east to west in storm (4)

indicatorNotes.moving east to west: the E (east) moves one place to the left, westward, in the word

blocks.note: GALE with its E shifted leftward

annotation.surface: A Celt travels westward through a storm.
annotation.walkthrough: In an across answer west is left, so the E of GALE shifts left past the L.
annotation.definitionFit: A Gael is a Gaelic-speaking Celt of Scotland or Ireland.

entries.clue: Prestissimo laps around here? (5)

indicatorNotes.around: the answer lies around the join of the words before it

annotation.surface: A question about where laps are driven very fast.
annotation.walkthrough: Prestissimo is the musical marking for 'as fast as possible'. Imola is an Italian motor-racing circuit, home of the San Marino Grand Prix, so the whole clue describes it.
annotation.definitionFit: Imola hosts very fast laps of Formula One racing.

entries.clue: Palace attendants in olde worlde horror film? (6)

annotation.surface: Royal servants appear in an old-fashioned scary movie.
annotation.walkthrough: The olde-worlde version of 'The Omen' is 'Ye Omen'. Yeomen of the Guard attend the British sovereign.
annotation.definitionFit: The Yeomen of the Guard are the monarch's ceremonial bodyguard at the palace.

entries.clue: Gasp at French eccentric's baggy trousers (10)

annotation.surface: Someone gasps at an odd Frenchman's baggy trousers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French eccentric' looks like one person, but 'at French' is A and 'eccentric's' is LOON'S.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: pantaloons were the loose breeches of the old stage clown Pantalone, and the word still means baggy trousers.

entries.clue: Sea arch (4)

blocks.note: poetic term for the open ocean, as in the Spanish ___

annotation.surface: An arch of rock standing in the sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sea arch' is a real coastal rock formation, but the two words split: arch is the adjective meaning principal.
annotation.definitionFit: The main is poetic for the ocean; main and arch both mean chief.

entries.clue: Expect caper, confusing it with pea (10)

indicatorNotes.confusing: IT and PEA are jumbled together

blocks.note: an antic is a playful caper

annotation.surface: Look forward to a caper, mixing it up with a pea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caper' could be the pickled bud next to 'pea', but here it is a prank, ANTIC.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to anticipate an event is to look forward to it as likely.

entries.clue: Criminal exercises persuasive charm over offences in court (9)

blocks.note: to tempt is to charm someone into something

annotation.surface: A crook sweet-talks people over his crimes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' belongs to the phrase for TEMPTS, not a reversal. Contempt of court is disrespecting or disobeying a court.
annotation.definitionFit: Contempt of court is the offence of defying or disrespecting a court.

entries.clue: Rocket engineer keeps pacing around Orpington, perhaps (10)

indicatorNotes.around: to pace around something is to walk on every side of it, so STEPS ON encircles HEN

blocks.note: Orpington is a breed of chicken

annotation.surface: An engineer keeps striding round a London suburb.
annotation.walkthrough: Orpington is a south-London suburb, but it is also a chicken breed: 'perhaps' flags it as an example of a HEN. George Stephenson built the Rocket locomotive.
annotation.definitionFit: George and Robert Stephenson engineered the Rocket, an early steam locomotive.

entries.clue: Favourite place to study a flower (7)

annotation.surface: A top spot for studying a bloom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Study a flower' reads as botany, but 'a' is just the letter A.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the petunia is one kind of flower, a trumpet-shaped bedding plant.

entries.clue: Text concise report on effectiveness of deodorant (4)

blocks.note: BO = body odour, the short name for it

annotation.surface: A short review of how well a deodorant works.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'concise report' is two abbreviations: the smell is BO and the verdict is OK.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: any written work, like a set text on a syllabus, is a book.

entries.clue: Unlimited fines given after German carmaker mixed hydrocarbons (7)

indicatorNotes.Unlimited: FINES loses its limits, its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.given after: placed after in reading order, as a thing given after another follows it, so INE follows BENZ

annotation.surface: A German car firm is fined heavily over its fuel blend.
annotation.walkthrough: Benzine is a volatile mixture of hydrocarbons from petroleum, which fits the car-fuel surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Benzine is a mixture of light hydrocarbons distilled from petroleum.

entries.clue: Trump, lying American (6)

annotation.surface: An accusation that the American president is a liar.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points at Donald Trump, but in British slang to trump is to break wind, and flatus is gas from the gut.
annotation.definitionFit: A trump, in British slang, is a fart, which is flatus.

entries.clue: Very cold hail in Olympic city one winter (5)

annotation.surface: Bitter hailstorms hit an Olympic host city one winter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hail' looks like icy weather but is a greeting, HI. Sochi, in Russia, hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the Russian Black Sea resort was the host city of the 2014 Winter Games.

entries.clue: Bard's work playing in theatre (5)

blocks.note: a show that is on is playing

annotation.surface: One of Shakespeare's plays is being performed at a theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: The Bard suggests Shakespeare and a play, but any bard, or poet, writes an ODE. Odeon is a British cinema chain, and an odeon was an ancient Greek theatre.
annotation.definitionFit: An odeon is a theatre, originally an ancient Greek hall for music.

entries.clue: Story of power and fate (4)

annotation.surface: A tale about power and destiny.
annotation.walkthrough: P for power is the physics symbol, and your lot in life is your fate.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the plot is the sequence of events a story tells.

entries.clue: Evil doctor going forwards and backwards in time (4)

indicatorNotes.going forwards and backwards: NO is written once going forwards as it stands, then going backwards as ON

annotation.surface: A wicked doctor travelling to and fro through time.
annotation.walkthrough: The time-travel picture is a decoy: Dr No is the villain of the first James Bond film.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: noon, twelve o'clock midday, is one particular time.

entries.clue: Cheese clubs are excited by Philadelphia (10)

indicatorNotes.excited: ARE is stirred into a new order

annotation.surface: A cheese-lovers' society gets thrilled by Philadelphia cream cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: Philadelphia is a brand of cream cheese, which pulls you toward the wrong cheese; here it is the city, Philly. Caerphilly is a crumbly white Welsh cheese.
annotation.definitionFit: Caerphilly is a mild, crumbly Welsh cheese.

entries.clue: Stop giving away old heart medication (6)

indicatorNotes.giving away: to give something away is to part with it, so STATION loses its O

blocks.note: a stop on a railway line

annotation.surface: Quit handing out outdated cardiac drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like an order to quit, but it is a noun: a station.
annotation.definitionFit: Statins are drugs that lower cholesterol to protect the heart.

entries.clue: Like American's money for half an Everest expedition? (6)

annotation.surface: An American asks about the cost of half an Everest trip.
annotation.walkthrough: An Everest expedition goes up and comes down; the ascent is the first half, and the question mark flags the looseness.
annotation.definitionFit: An expedition climbs up and then descends; the ascent is half of it.
